nodes.summary: The point $A = (0, 0)$, the origin of the coordinate plane; it is the right-angle vertex of the triangle in Hippocrates' theorem on lunes.
nodes.title: Right-angle vertex of the lune triangle

nodes.summary: For a real number $a$, the point $B = (a, 0)$ on the $x$-axis of the coordinate plane; it is the endpoint of the horizontal leg of the right triangle in Hippocrates' theorem on lunes.
nodes.title: Horizontal leg endpoint of the lune triangle

nodes.summary: For a real number $b$, the point $C = (0, b)$ on the $y$-axis of the coordinate plane; it is the endpoint of the vertical leg of the right triangle in Hippocrates' theorem on lunes.
nodes.title: Vertical leg endpoint of the lune triangle

nodes.summary: Given points $p$ and $q$ of the coordinate plane and a property $S$ of real numbers, this is the set of points $x$ such that the squared Euclidean distance from $x$ to the midpoint of $p$ and $q$ is at most one quarter of the squared Euclidean distance from $p$ to $q$ (so $x$ lies in the closed disk with diameter $pq$), and $S$ holds of the planar determinant $\det(q - p, x - p)$. For $p \ne q$, taking $S(t)$ to be…
nodes.title: Closed half-disk on a diameter

nodes.summary: For vectors $u = (u_1, u_2)$ and $v = (v_1, v_2)$ of the coordinate plane, $\det(u, v) = u_1 v_2 - u_2 v_1$, the signed area of the parallelogram spanned by $u$ and $v$.
nodes.title: Planar determinant for Hippocrates' lunes

nodes.summary: For points $p = (p_1, p_2)$ and $q = (q_1, q_2)$ of the coordinate plane, the squared Euclidean distance between them is $(p_1 - q_1)^2 + (p_2 - q_2)^2$.
nodes.title: Squared Euclidean distance in the plane

nodes.summary: Let $a, b > 0$ and consider the right triangle with vertices $A = (0, 0)$, $B = (a, 0)$ and $C = (0, b)$. The Lebesgue measure of the lune on the horizontal leg plus the Lebesgue measure of the lune on the vertical leg equals the Lebesgue measure of the triangle, that is, of the convex hull of $A$, $B$ and $C$.
nodes.title: Hippocrates' theorem on lunes

nodes.summary: For real numbers $a$ and $b$, let $A = (0, 0)$, $B = (a, 0)$ and $C = (0, b)$. The lune on the horizontal leg is the set of points $x = (x_1, x_2)$ of the closed disk with diameter $AB$ satisfying $a x_2 \le 0$ that do not lie in the half-disk on the hypotenuse, the set of points of the closed disk with diameter $BC$ satisfying $b x_1 + a x_2 \le ab$. For $a, b > 0$ this is the set of points of the closed lower…
nodes.title: Lune on the horizontal leg

nodes.summary: For real numbers $a$ and $b$, let $B = (a, 0)$ and $C = (0, b)$. The half-disk on the hypotenuse is the set of points $x = (x_1, x_2)$ of the closed disk with diameter $BC$ satisfying $\det(C - B, x - B) \ge 0$, that is, $b x_1 + a x_2 \le ab$. For $a, b > 0$ this is the half of the disk on the side of the line $BC$ containing the right-angle vertex $(0, 0)$.
nodes.title: Half-disk on the hypotenuse

nodes.summary: For points $p = (p_1, p_2)$ and $q = (q_1, q_2)$ of the coordinate plane, their midpoint is $\left(\frac{p_1 + q_1}{2}, \frac{p_2 + q_2}{2}\right)$.
nodes.title: Midpoint of two points in the plane

nodes.summary: The coordinate plane is the set $\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}$ of ordered pairs $(x, y)$ of real numbers.
nodes.title: Coordinate plane for Hippocrates' lunes

nodes.summary: For real numbers $a$ and $b$, the right triangle $T(a, b)$ is the convex hull in the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ of the three points $(0, 0)$, $(a, 0)$ and $(0, b)$.
nodes.title: Right triangle with legs on the axes

nodes.summary: For points $p = (p_1, p_2)$ and $q = (q_1, q_2)$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$, the displacement vector from $p$ to $q$ is $(q_1 - p_1, q_2 - p_2)$.
nodes.title: Displacement vector between two points of the plane

nodes.summary: For real numbers $a$ and $b$, the vertical lune is the set of points $(x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^2$ with $x^2 + (y - b/2)^2 \le b^2/4$ and $bx \le 0$ that do not satisfy both $(x - a/2)^2 + (y - b/2)^2 \le (a^2 + b^2)/4$ and $bx + ay \le ab$.
nodes.title: Hippocrates lune on the vertical leg

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
